decision: Which approach best resolves: WF-078 requires a recipient to prove identity before a document opens or before it is signed, and records every attempt in the audit trail. The e-signature workflow (WF-095) cites the same verification object and says identity verification 'is enabled per-workspace (passcode, SMS, KBA, ID check)'. Both specs name the same thing. Exactly one workflow may own the setting so the gate is not implemented twice. Which workflow owns it?

state.problem: WF-078 requires a recipient to prove identity before a document opens or before it is signed, and records every attempt in the audit trail. The e-signature workflow (WF-095) cites the same verification object and says identity verification 'is enabled per-workspace (passcode, SMS, KBA, ID check)'. Both specs name the same thing. Exactly one workflow may own the setting so the gate is not implemented twice. Which workflow owns it?

candidate_solutions.wf078_owns_gate: WF-078 owns the verification settings object on the recipient, the two axes (method as a discriminated union: passcode / phone SMS / KBA / ID; timing as a separate axis: before_open / before_sign), the passcode and E.164 validation, the attempt evaluation, and the withholding of the document body. WF-095 reads the setting and sends the request; it does not enforce it.
candidate_solutions.wf095_owns_gate: WF-095 owns the setting because it owns the document and recipient records the setting lives on. WF-078 becomes a read-only reporter that reads whatever verification_settings it finds and evaluates attempts against them.
candidate_solutions.shared_rule_module: Neither workflow owns it alone. The rule moves into a shared module both import, so the gate has one implementation and neither ticket owns it.
candidate_solutions.wf078_owns_gate_workflow_keyed: WF-078 owns the setting and enforces it, and the setting is keyed per workflow rather than per workspace, so a workspace can require one verification before opening and a different one before signing without the two settings colliding.

context.wf095_note: WF-095 is not implemented in this repository. Nothing imports it, so a design that delegates enforcement to it cannot be tested and cannot be reviewed.

observed_evidence.pandadoc_object: Add verification_settings to a recipient either at document creation or on an existing document. Method table: passcode_verification.passcode 'must be 6-100 characters with at least one letter and one digit'; phone_verification.phone_number 'must be in international format (e.g., +1555667890)'; kba_verification.enabled 'The recipient answers identity questions generated from public records'; id_verification.enabled 'The recipient verifies identity with a government-issued ID'. Timing: before_open = 'Before the recipient can view the document' / 'All recipients'; before_sign = 'Before the recipient can sign' / 'Signers only'.
observed_evidence.audit_codes: 47 recipient verification with kba passed; 51 recipient verification with kba failed; 69 recipient verification with email otp passed; 70 recipient verification with email otp failed. Codes 47-54 are the verification band.
observed_evidence.automation: Verification is re-asserted by the gate on every attempt; there is no 'verify once, remember forever' behaviour. Both success and failure produce audit actions, so a rejected attempt is as visible as a successful one.
observed_evidence.data_flow: Verification config is persisted on the recipient record. At the chosen gate the recipient's identity is proven out of band and the result is stamped onto the recipient's session; the document body is withheld until it clears.
observed_evidence.already_in_this_repository: dsr/audit_export/vocabulary.py already owns the integer action-code vocabulary and already lays out codes 47-50 as four pass codes and 51-54 as four fail codes, with the method order (kba, passcode, sms, id). It is the only place a verification code is defined, and it is WF-079's.

requirements: The feature adds files and edits no shared file.
Every write goes through AuditedDatabase so the audit row lands in the same transaction.
Records are ordinary JSON in records.data. No migration and no typed column.
The setting, the two axes, the passcode bound, the E.164 bound and the attempt audit must all be enforceable and testable in this repository on its own.
A team adding a field must need no coordination with anyone.
constraints: The four domain packages available to extend are crm_integration, throttle, lead_score, visitor_identification, lead_qualification, round_robin and concierge_router. dsr/security_governance exists and is WF-073's.
A feature may not import another feature module.
The integer code vocabulary belongs to dsr.audit_export.vocabulary and must not be minted a second time.
